lit: so alarmed and flustered that one loses all sense of what to do

use.how: Predicate, or adverbial with 地: 他惊慌失措地跑了出去。 Describes a frightened reaction to sudden danger or shocking news; often in 不要惊慌失措.

near.diff: 手忙脚乱 is a frantic, disorganised rush, often just from being busy; 惊慌失措 is panic caused by fear or shock.
不知所措 is being at a loss what to do, from confusion or embarrassment; 惊慌失措 adds fright and panic.

cue: The ship suddenly lurches and the alarm sounds; passengers scream and run in all directions, too frightened to think. How do they react?

ctx.s: 听到火警响了，几个孩子{惊慌失措}地跑出了教室。
ctx.en: When the fire alarm went off, a few children ran out of the classroom in a panic.

ctx.s: 遇到地震时千万不要{惊慌失措}，先躲到桌子下面。
ctx.en: If there is an earthquake, whatever you do, don't panic; get under a table first.

ctx.s: 飞机突然剧烈颠簸，乘客们{惊慌失措}，空姐却很镇定。
ctx.en: The plane suddenly shook violently; the passengers panicked, but the flight attendant stayed calm.

ctx.s: “你刚才怎么那么{惊慌失措}？”“我以为钱包被偷了。”
ctx.en: "Why were you in such a panic just now?" "I thought my wallet had been stolen."

ctx.s: 突然停电了，值班经理没有{惊慌失措}，马上启动了备用电源。
ctx.en: The power suddenly went out; the duty manager didn't panic and switched on the backup supply at once.

ctx.s: 看到他{惊慌失措}的样子，我就知道出大事了。
ctx.en: When I saw how panic-stricken he looked, I knew something serious had happened.

bad.s: 明天就要考试了，我{惊慌失措}地复习了一整夜。
bad.en: (meant: I was nervous and revised all night before the exam)
bad.why: It is a sudden panic in the face of danger or a shock, not ongoing nervousness while working; say you revised nervously (jǐnzhāng) instead.

bad.s: 收到录取通知书，她高兴得{惊慌失措}。
bad.en: (meant: she was beside herself with joy at the acceptance letter)
bad.why: The panic comes from fear or alarm, never from happiness; for joy, say she jumped for joy (gāoxìng de tiào le qǐlai).

use.how: Adverbial before a verb, or attributive with 的: 他无缘无故发脾气。 Often in complaints, or in 不会无缘无故… (there must be a reason).

near.diff: 莫名其妙 says something baffles the speaker and makes no sense; 无缘无故 states that an action or event had no cause.

cue: Your manager cancels your approved leave, gives no cause, and nothing you did could explain it. How did he cancel it?

ctx.s: 我又没惹他，他今天却{无缘无故}冲我发了一通火。
ctx.en: I hadn't done anything to him, yet today he blew up at me for no reason at all.

ctx.s: 陌生人{无缘无故}送的礼物，我是不会收的。
ctx.en: I won't accept a gift a stranger gives me for no reason.

ctx.s: 老板不会{无缘无故}请你吃饭，肯定有事要说。
ctx.en: The boss wouldn't take you to dinner for nothing; he must have something to tell you.

ctx.s: “你为什么打他？”“我可不是{无缘无故}动手的，是他先骂人的。”
ctx.en: "Why did you hit him?" "I didn't hit him for no reason; he insulted me first."

ctx.s: 扣工资总得有个理由，公司不能{无缘无故}就扣。
ctx.en: Docking pay needs a reason; the company can't just dock it for nothing.

ctx.s: 一个好好的孩子，怎么会{无缘无故}不肯上学呢？
ctx.en: How could a perfectly normal child suddenly refuse to go to school for no reason?

bad.s: 我{无缘无故}地在街上遇到了老同学。
bad.en: (meant: I happened to run into an old classmate on the street)
bad.why: It means an action had no cause, usually a puzzling or unfair one, not a lucky coincidence; say pèngqiǎo or ǒurán.

bad.s: 这道题{无缘无故}，我完全看不懂。
bad.en: (meant: this problem makes no sense to me)
bad.why: It describes an action or event that lacks a cause, not something confusing to read; call the problem baffling (mò míng qí miào).

mean: only natural; as a matter of course
lit: as reason says it ought to be

use.how: Predicate with 是…的, adverbial with 地, or in 把…看作理所当然 (to take for granted). Says something is right and to be expected by reason or duty.

cue: Your flatmate expects you to clean up after him every day and never says thanks, as if it were simply your job. How does he see your help?

ctx.s: 借了别人的钱，按时还是{理所当然}的事。
ctx.en: If you borrow money, paying it back on time is only natural.

ctx.s: 他是队里跑得最快的，{理所当然}地被选去参加比赛。
ctx.en: He was the fastest runner on the team, so naturally he was picked for the race.

ctx.s: 很多孩子把父母的付出看作{理所当然}。
ctx.en: Many children take everything their parents do for them for granted.

ctx.s: “你帮了我这么多，真不知道怎么谢你。”“朋友之间互相帮忙，{理所当然}嘛。”
ctx.en: "You've helped me so much, I don't know how to thank you." "Friends help each other; it goes without saying."

ctx.s: 违约就要赔偿，这是{理所当然}的，没什么好争的。
ctx.en: If you break the contract you pay compensation; that's a matter of course, nothing to argue about.

ctx.s: 他是公司的创始人，大家{理所当然}地推选他当董事长。
ctx.en: He founded the company, so naturally everyone elected him chairman.

bad.s: 我今天又{理所当然}地忘了带钥匙。
bad.en: (meant: of course I forgot my keys again today)
bad.why: It says something is right and justified by reason or duty; it cannot carry the rueful English 'of course' about a slip. Say 'yòu wàng le' alone.

bad.s: 我们不应该{理所当然}父母的照顾。
bad.en: (meant: we shouldn't take our parents' care for granted)
bad.why: It is not a verb and takes no object; use the pattern bǎ … kànzuò lǐ suǒ dāng rán (to take … for granted).

lit: cannot be grasped by thought or put into words

story.text: The phrase began as a Buddhist term. In the sutras it described the wisdom and powers of the Buddhas as so profound that they could not be reached by thinking (sī) or by discussion (yì). In everyday Chinese it widened to mean anything so astonishing that it seems impossible.
story.source: 佛经用语，如《维摩诘经·不思议品》

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 真是不可思议 / 不可思议的事. Expresses amazement that something seems impossible, good or bad.

near.diff: 莫名其妙 is being baffled, often annoyed, by something that makes no sense; 不可思议 is amazement at something that seems impossible.

cue: A tiny ant carries a leaf many times its own weight straight up a wall, and your friend stares, amazed it is even possible. What does she say?

ctx.s: 这么小的手机能拍出这么清楚的照片，真是{不可思议}！
ctx.en: A phone this small can take such sharp photos; it's incredible!

ctx.s: 一个十岁的孩子能背下整本字典？太{不可思议}了。
ctx.en: A ten-year-old who can recite a whole dictionary? That's unbelievable.

ctx.s: 他从十楼掉下来居然只受了点轻伤，医生都觉得{不可思议}。
ctx.en: He fell from the tenth floor and was only slightly hurt; even the doctors found it hard to believe.

ctx.s: “我在纽约街头碰到了小学同学。”“真的？太{不可思议}了！”
ctx.en: "I ran into a primary-school classmate on a street in New York." "Really? That's incredible!"

ctx.s: 宇宙中还有许多{不可思议}的现象等着科学家去解释。
ctx.en: The universe still holds many astonishing phenomena waiting for scientists to explain.

ctx.s: 回想起来，我们几个人开着一辆旧车穿过了沙漠，至今仍觉得{不可思议}。
ctx.en: Looking back, a few of us crossed the desert in an old car; I still find it hard to believe.

bad.s: 他说话{不可思议}，大家都听不懂。
bad.en: (meant: he talks so confusingly that nobody understands him)
bad.why: It expresses amazement at something that seems impossible, not that someone's speech is unclear or hard to follow.

bad.s: 这个问题你先{不可思议}一下，再回答我。
bad.en: (meant: think this question over first, then answer me)
bad.why: Sīyì here is part of a fixed adjective meaning inconceivable; it is not a verb for thinking something over. Say kǎolǜ yīxià.

use.how: Sentence-initial 众所周知，… or 是众所周知的 / 众所周知的事实. Introduces a fact the public or the audience already knows, in speeches, articles and reports.

cue: Opening a talk, you want to remind the audience of a fact every one of them already knows before you build your argument on it. How do you begin?

ctx.s: {众所周知}，吸烟对身体有害。
ctx.en: As everyone knows, smoking is bad for your health.

ctx.s: 长城是中国的象征，这是{众所周知}的。
ctx.en: It is common knowledge that the Great Wall is a symbol of China.

ctx.s: {众所周知}，这家公司的产品以质量好而闻名。
ctx.en: As is well known, this company's products are famous for their quality.

ctx.s: 在发布会上，经理说：“{众所周知}，今年的市场竞争非常激烈。”
ctx.en: At the press conference the manager said, "As we all know, competition in the market is very fierce this year."

ctx.s: 他常常迟到，这在公司里是{众所周知}的事。
ctx.en: His lateness is common knowledge in the company.

ctx.s: 并非所有{众所周知}的说法都经得起科学的检验。
ctx.en: Not every well-known claim stands up to scientific testing.

bad.s: {众所周知}，我昨天晚上吃了饺子。
bad.en: (meant: well, last night I had dumplings)
bad.why: It introduces a fact the public widely knows; using it for a private detail nobody could know sounds absurd.

bad.s: 他{众所周知}了这件事。
bad.en: (meant: everyone came to know about it)
bad.why: It is not a verb with a person as subject; it describes the fact itself as known to all, so the matter must be the subject.

lit: one look and everything is clear

use.how: Predicate: 图表一目了然 / 让人一目了然. Said of how something is presented or shown: a chart, sign, layout or result that needs only one look.

near.diff: 一目了然 is about something being easy to see at one look; 一清二楚 is about knowing, remembering or explaining every detail.

cue: The new dashboard puts every key figure on one screen, so anyone grasps the situation the moment they look at it. How is it laid out?

ctx.s: 这张地图画得很好，路线{一目了然}。
ctx.en: This map is well drawn; the route is clear at a glance.

ctx.s: 把数据做成图表，变化趋势就{一目了然}了。
ctx.en: Put the data in a chart and the trend is obvious at a glance.

ctx.s: 新菜单把价格和配料都列了出来，让顾客{一目了然}。
ctx.en: The new menu lists the prices and ingredients so customers can see everything at a glance.

ctx.s: “这个网站好用吗？”“好用，所有功能都在首页，{一目了然}。”
ctx.en: "Is the website easy to use?" "Yes, all the features are on the home page; you see them at a glance."

ctx.s: 车站的指示牌设计得{一目了然}，第一次来的人也不会走错。
ctx.en: The station signs are so clear that even first-time visitors don't go the wrong way.

ctx.s: 报告用红绿两色标出了各部门的业绩，好坏{一目了然}。
ctx.en: The report marks each department's results in red or green, so good and bad are clear at a glance.

bad.s: 那件事过去十年了，他还记得{一目了然}。
bad.en: (meant: ten years on, he still remembers it in every detail)
bad.why: It describes something visible at one look, not a person's detailed memory or knowledge; say yī qīng èr chǔ.

bad.s: 我看了他一眼，就{一目了然}地爱上了他。
bad.en: (meant: I fell in love with him at first sight)
bad.why: It means something is clear at a glance, not at first sight; love at first sight is yī jiàn zhōng qíng.

mean: knowing or seeing every detail clearly

use.how: Complement after 得 (记得、看得、说得、查得一清二楚) or predicate: 我心里一清二楚. About how fully someone knows, remembers or explains a matter.

near.diff: 一目了然 is about something being easy to see at one look; 一清二楚 is about knowing or explaining a matter in full detail.

cue: The detective can tell you exactly where the suspect was at every minute that night, down to the smallest detail. How well does the detective know it?

ctx.s: 那天发生的事，我到现在还记得{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: I still remember every detail of what happened that day.

ctx.s: 老师把考试要求讲得{一清二楚}，没人再问问题。
ctx.en: The teacher explained the exam requirements so clearly that nobody had any more questions.

ctx.s: 你别想骗我，你昨晚去哪儿了我{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: Don't try to fool me; I know exactly where you went last night.

ctx.s: 警察很快就把事情的经过调查得{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: The police soon found out exactly how it had all happened.

ctx.s: “合同上的条款你都看明白了吗？”“放心，每一条我都看得{一清二楚}。”
ctx.en: "Did you understand all the terms in the contract?" "Don't worry, I understood every one of them perfectly."

ctx.s: 他在这条街上住了三十年，哪家店卖什么，他心里{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: He has lived on this street for thirty years and knows exactly which shop sells what.

bad.s: 今天天空{一清二楚}，一点云都没有。
bad.en: (meant: the sky is clear today, without a cloud)
bad.why: It is about knowing or explaining a matter in detail, not about clear weather; a cloudless sky is qínglǎng.

bad.s: 他是个{一清二楚}的人，从来不撒谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is an honest, upright person who never lies)
bad.why: It describes how clearly something is known, not a person's honesty; say chéngshí (honest).

lit: in a flash, a great awakening of understanding

use.how: Predicate without an object, often 才恍然大悟 or 恍然大悟地说; usually followed by 原来…. Said when something that puzzled you suddenly makes sense.

near.diff: 大开眼界 is seeing new things that broaden your experience; 恍然大悟 is suddenly understanding something that had puzzled you.

cue: For weeks you couldn't work out why your plants kept dying; then you notice the window faces north, and in that instant it all makes sense. What happens?

ctx.s: 听他这么一说，我{恍然大悟}，原来是我记错了时间。
ctx.en: When he said that, it suddenly dawned on me: I had got the time wrong.

ctx.s: 看到桌上的蛋糕，他{恍然大悟}：原来今天是自己的生日。
ctx.en: Seeing the cake on the table, he suddenly realised that today was his own birthday.

ctx.s: 这道题我想了一个晚上，第二天刷牙时才{恍然大悟}。
ctx.en: I puzzled over this problem all evening, and it only clicked the next morning while I was brushing my teeth.

ctx.s: 直到读到最后一页，读者才{恍然大悟}，凶手就是那个管家。
ctx.en: Only on the last page does the reader suddenly realise the butler was the murderer.

ctx.s: 她{恍然大悟}地拍了拍脑袋：“难怪钥匙找不到，我放在车里了！”
ctx.en: She slapped her forehead as it dawned on her: "No wonder I couldn't find my keys, I left them in the car!"

ctx.s: 很多年后，他才{恍然大悟}，父亲当年的严厉其实是一种爱。
ctx.en: Only many years later did he realise that his father's strictness had been a kind of love.

bad.s: 我今天在课上{恍然大悟}了很多新单词。
bad.en: (meant: I learned a lot of new words in class today)
bad.why: It is a sudden insight into something that puzzled you, not learning new material, and it takes no object.

bad.s: 他早上七点{恍然大悟}，起床去上班。
bad.en: (meant: he woke up at seven and got up for work)
bad.why: Wù is waking up to the truth in the mind, not waking from sleep; say xǐnglái.

lit: to greatly widen the field of one's eyes

use.how: Predicate, often 让人大开眼界 or 真是大开眼界. Said after seeing or experiencing something new and impressive that widens one's horizons.

near.diff: 恍然大悟 is suddenly understanding something that puzzled you; 大开眼界 is seeing new things you had never seen before.

cue: On your first visit to a huge robot factory, you see machines doing things you had never imagined. How does the visit leave you?

ctx.s: 这次去博物馆参观，孩子们都{大开眼界}。
ctx.en: The museum visit was a real eye-opener for the children.

ctx.s: 这场科技展览让我{大开眼界}，原来机器人已经会做饭了。
ctx.en: The technology fair opened my eyes; robots can already cook!

ctx.s: 在国外交流的一年让她{大开眼界}，也更了解自己的国家了。
ctx.en: Her exchange year abroad broadened her horizons and also helped her understand her own country better.

ctx.s: “昨天的魔术表演怎么样？”“太精彩了，真让人{大开眼界}！”
ctx.en: "How was the magic show yesterday?" "Amazing, a real eye-opener!"

ctx.s: 跟着老渔民出海一天，城里来的学生们{大开眼界}。
ctx.en: After a day at sea with an old fisherman, the students from the city had seen a whole new world.

ctx.s: 这本书介绍了深海里各种奇特的生物，读来令人{大开眼界}。
ctx.en: This book describes all kinds of strange deep-sea creatures; it is an eye-opening read.

bad.s: 他终于{大开眼界}，明白了自己错在哪里。
bad.en: (meant: he finally realised where he had gone wrong)
bad.why: It means seeing new things that widen one's experience, not suddenly understanding a mistake; say huǎng rán dà wù.

bad.s: 早上醒来，我{大开眼界}，看了看手机。
bad.en: (meant: I woke up, opened my eyes and checked my phone)
bad.why: It is never about physically opening one's eyes; say zhēngkāi yǎnjing.

lit: gathering it all together and saying it

use.how: Sentence-initial connector after several points have been made: 总而言之，… Sums up what was said, in speech or writing.

cue: After listing the pros and cons of three phones at length, you are about to give your final verdict in one sentence. What phrase introduces it?

ctx.s: 这家店菜好吃，价格也便宜，{总而言之}，值得一去。
ctx.en: The food here is good and the prices are low; all in all, it's worth a visit.

ctx.s: 我们讨论了一下午，{总而言之}，方案下周一前必须交。
ctx.en: We've discussed it all afternoon; in short, the plan has to be handed in by Monday.

ctx.s: “这房子离公司远，房租又贵，{总而言之}，我不想租。”
ctx.en: "This flat is far from work and the rent is high; in a word, I don't want it."

ctx.s: {总而言之}，只要大家齐心协力，就没有解决不了的问题。
ctx.en: In conclusion, as long as we all pull together, there is no problem we can't solve.

ctx.s: 有人说早起好，有人说睡够了更好，{总而言之}，适合自己最重要。
ctx.en: Some say getting up early is best, others say enough sleep matters more; in the end, what suits you is what counts.

ctx.s: 文章最后写道：{总而言之}，保护环境需要每个人的参与。
ctx.en: The article ends: in short, protecting the environment needs everyone to take part.

bad.s: {总而言之}，大家好，今天我来介绍一下我们的新产品。
bad.en: (meant: to begin, hello everyone, today I'll present our new product)
bad.why: It sums up what has already been said, so it cannot open a talk; start with shǒuxiān or just the greeting.

bad.s: 他在会上{总而言之}讲了三个小时。
bad.en: (meant: altogether he spoke for three hours at the meeting)
bad.why: It is a connector that sums up points already made, not an adverb meaning altogether or in total; say yígòng.
